decisions.decision: Open with the thing a Rust developer recognises: a dependency pinned to an exact version, a lock held across an await, a test that builds its own fixture.
decisions.rationale: It now opens with the thing a Rust developer recognises: a dependency pinned to an exact version, a lock held across an await, a test that builds its own fixture. Each was a decision resting on something true at the time, none of it in the code, and some of it in a commit message that cannot be queried and never says when the ground under it moved.
decisions.quote: It now opens with the thing a Rust developer recognises: a dependency pinned to an exact version, a lock held across an await, a test that builds its own fixture.

decisions.decision: Show what the tool does rather than describe it.
decisions.rationale: Then what the tool does, shown rather than described, with real output from this repository: one commit read back with its rejected alternative beside it, and `stale` naming the functions that have changed under recorded reasoning.
decisions.quote: Then what the tool does, shown rather than described, with real output from this repository:

decisions.decision: Drop the claim of answering 'why is this like this?' as a product feature.
decisions.rationale: Answering "why is this like this?" was dropped as a product claim.
decisions.quote: Answering "why is this like this?" was dropped as a product claim.

decisions.decision: Assign labels, sources and statuses; the model proposes wording only.
decisions.rationale: The tool assigns labels, sources and statuses; the model proposes wording only. Every quote is checked against the commit, and an absent quote caps its unit at `speculative`.
decisions.quote: The tool assigns labels, sources and statuses; the model proposes wording only.

decisions.decision: Detect staleness by item body hash rather than line ranges.
decisions.rationale: Staleness is attached to code identity rather than to line ranges, so a function that moved is not stale and one that changed is.

decisions.decision: Record review as confirmations, withdrawals with reasons, and closures with notes.
decisions.rationale: Review as records. Confirming writes an attestation, rejecting writes a withdrawal whose reason unit says why, closing writes a resolution. The log keeps everything.

decisions.decision: Ship its own instrument for benchmarking the model.
decisions.rationale: It ships its own instrument. `bench` measures the model *you* chose on *your* commits, and every published figure names the model it came from — including four experiments that failed and are listed so nobody repeats them.

decisions.decision: Focus on deterministic commands over model-dependent ones.
decisions.rationale: Two thirds of the commands never call a model. Those are the ones worth your time today: they are deterministic, tested, and cost nothing to run.
decisions.quote: Two thirds of the commands never call a model.

decisions.decision: Publish figures naming the model each came from, including failed experiments.
decisions.rationale: The figures are published, naming the model each came from, including the experiments that failed. The rest of this document is that account — written for someone deciding whether to spend an afternoon on this, and reviewing the tool as it was built rather than as it was designed.
decisions.quote: The figures are published, naming the model each came from, including the experiments that failed.

decisions.decision: Highlight over-production as the failure mode that matters.
decisions.rationale: Over-production is the failure mode that matters. A corpus of 54 decisions for a four-decision commit is worse than no corpus, and prompt wording was measured twice as not being the lever.
decisions.quote: Over-production is the failure mode that matters.

decisions.decision: Meaningfully price extraction runs before starting them.
decisions.rationale: The hook only queues and `--estimate` prices a run before it starts.
decisions.quote: The hook only queues and `--estimate` prices a run before it starts.

decisions.decision: Label cloned corpora as someone else's claims.
decisions.rationale: A cloned corpus is someone else's claim. Units carry the status the tool gave them; read `speculative` as what it says.
decisions.quote: A cloned corpus is someone else's claim.
